studies.name: Hunt X, Saran A, White H, Kuper H. Effectiveness of interventions for improving educational outcomes for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2025;21:e70016.
studies.draft_uses: Full 2025 publication: 28 studies analysed; significant effects on literacy, cognitive skills, handwriting, numeracy; all but one study rated low confidence; most interventions targeted individual children; no studies in humanitarian settings; few disaggregated by gender; high heterogeneity; 18 studies on 'Skills for learning' of which 12 had significant effects; 'Conditions for inclusion' showed moderately significant effect; 'Accessible learning environments' second most common category.
studies.latest_known: Published February 6, 2025, Campbell Systematic Reviews 21(1):e70016. No correction or update found as of November 2026. The search cut-off for the review was March 2022.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed; this is the most recent and only full version of this review.

studies.name: Saran A, White H, Kuper H. Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness of interventions for people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2020;16(1):e1070.
studies.draft_uses: Studies focus on 'fixing individuals'; absence of evidence on disability inclusion called 'a very striking gap'; over half of impact evaluations came from upper-middle income countries; only nine from low-income countries.
studies.latest_known: Corrigendum published July 12, 2020 (Campbell Systematic Reviews 16(3):e1104, DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1104). The corrigendum corrected the income-country distribution figure: the original text 'over half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from upper-middle income countries' was changed to 'almost half (n=50) the impact evaluations come from lower-middle income countries, closely followed by upper-middle income countries (n=48).' The figure for low-income countries (n=9) was retained.
studies.what_changed: The draft states 'over half of the impact evaluations came from upper-middle income countries' — this is the pre-corrigendum wording. The corrigendum (July 2020) changed this to 'almost half' from lower-middle income countries (n=50), with upper-middle income countries second (n=48). The draft's characterisation of the income-country distribution is therefore wrong: it attributes the 'over half' share to upper-middle income countries, whereas the corrected text assigns it to lower-middle income countries. The figure for low-income countries (n=9) is unaffected.

studies.name: Kuper H, Saran A, White H. Rapid Evidence Assessment (REA) of What Works to Improve Educational Outcomes for People with Disabilities in Low- and Middle-Income Countries. Campbell Collaboration and International Centre for Evidence in Disability. 2018.
studies.draft_uses: The draft explicitly states it could not hold this source and that nothing on the page draws on it. The source is listed in the bibliography only.
studies.latest_known: The 2018 REA was a precursor to the 2025 Hunt et al. systematic review, which PubMed records as an update of the associated protocol. No separate update to the REA itself was found; it has been functionally superseded by the 2025 full systematic review.
studies.what_changed: The draft draws no figures from this source, so no draft claim is affected. The REA is superseded as a body of evidence by the 2025 Hunt et al. systematic review, but because the draft correctly excludes it, this supersession does not introduce any error into the draft.

studies.name: Ahmed SK, Jeffries D, Chakraborty A, et al. Teacher professional development for disability inclusion in low- and middle-income Asia-Pacific countries: An evidence and gap map. Campbell Systematic Reviews. 2022;18(4):e1287.
studies.draft_uses: 50 studies from 16 of 41 LMIC countries in Asia-Pacific; significant number of interventions focus on changing teacher attitudes and understanding of disability; only three studies address mental health of students with disability; no studies on how teachers could support positive student behaviour; qualitative study from Vietnam on training seminars and workshops; no interventions supporting students during emergency or crisis situations.
studies.latest_known: A corrigendum (e1315, DOI: 10.1002/cl2.1315) was published February 25, 2023 (Campbell Systematic Reviews 19(1):e1315). The draft itself acknowledges this correction exists but states it could not read it. Despite this, the draft proceeds to cite multiple specific figures from the uncorrected version of the map. The content of the corrigendum could not be fully retrieved from available search results, so it is not possible to confirm whether the specific figures the draft uses (50 studies, 16 countries, three mental health studies, no positive-behaviour studies) were among those corrected.
studies.what_changed: Cannot confirm which figures changed. The draft states it draws nothing from this source due to the unread correction, but in practice it cites at least six specific figures and findings from it. All of those figures must be treated as unverified against the corrected version. The draft's disclaimer ('nothing on this page draws on it') is inconsistent with its actual content, which repeatedly attributes findings to source [4].
